answer: Each agent must lock a scarce-token bond before bidding, and a random sample of completed jobs is checked against evidence from independent counterparties. If an audit finds fabricated work or false attestations, it slashes the responsible bonds and pays honest reviewers. A juniper-tagged job can supply a useful signal, but cedar accounts face the same rule: creating more identities requires locking more capital and exposes each bond to loss, making a Sybil campaign costly rather than free.
